result.summary: The street environment is characterized by inconsistent pedestrian infrastructure, with a well-defined sidewalk on the right but a degraded, poorly defined walkway on the left that is partially used for informal parking. The lack of marked crossings and traffic calming measures, combined with blank frontages, creates a relatively hostile environment for pedestrians despite the low-speed urban context.

hazards.name: Degraded and Obstructed Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left side of the image is unpaved or severely degraded and is being used for informal vehicle parking, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked pedestrian crossings visible, which is hazardous given the commercial activity (food shop) on the right.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars on both sides of the street limit sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction and Definition
interventions.description: Pave and clearly define the sidewalk on the left side of the street with a raised curb to prevent vehicle encroachment.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks, particularly near the commercial storefront, to provide a designated and visible crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a narrow sidewalk that is significantly obstructed by a large dumpster and barrels, creating a constrained path. The adjacent building has a blank frontage with boarded windows, providing no natural surveillance or buffer from the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A large dumpster and several barrels occupy a significant portion of the narrow sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to maneuver around them or potentially step into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left and center-right on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the narrow sidewalk and the active travel lane, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The building at the sidewalk level features a long blank wall and boarded windows, which reduces natural surveillance and can make the environment feel less safe for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance and Management
interventions.description: Relocate the dumpster and barrels to a designated off-street area or a curbside flex zone to ensure a continuous, unobstructed clear path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extension or Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Implement a curb extension or a painted/physical buffer zone with bollards or planters to provide more space for pedestrians and separate them from moving traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during evening hours, especially given the lack of active frontage.

result.summary: The street features narrow sidewalks on both sides with parallel parking that creates visual barriers between pedestrians and the roadway. There is a lack of marked crossings, traffic calming measures, and pedestrian-scale lighting, while utility poles obstruct the already limited walking space.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the path of the narrow sidewalk on the left, forcing pedestrians to maneuver around them.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or curb ramps are visible, making it difficult and unsafe for pedestrians to cross the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint high-visibility crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the road, while also naturally slowing traffic speeds.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Obstacle Removal
interventions.description: Widen sidewalks and relocate utility poles to provide a clear, unobstructed path for all users, including those with mobility aids.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly degraded by large amounts of trash and debris obstructing the sidewalk. The lack of maintenance, combined with cracked pavement and blank building frontages, creates a hostile and neglected atmosphere for walking.

hazards.name: Accumulated trash and debris
hazards.description: Large amounts of litter and bulk waste block the sidewalk and spill from the adjacent lot, creating significant trip hazards and forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right of the image, on the sidewalk and in the gap between buildings.

hazards.name: Cracked and uneven sidewalk
hazards.description: The concrete sidewalk panels are cracked and uneven, which can cause trips or falls, especially for those with mobility impairments.

interventions.title: Sanitation and debris removal
interventions.description: Regular maintenance to clear the sidewalk of trash and bulk waste is essential for restoring a safe walking path.

interventions.title: Sidewalk repair and leveling
interventions.description: Replacing damaged concrete panels to ensure a smooth, continuous, and ADA-compliant walking surface.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-scale street lighting
interventions.description: Adding lighting would improve visibility and the perception of safety in this neglected mid-block section.
